messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: high egress errors for customer Orchard (vpc-private, dedicated). Alert: NLB 5xx rate spike + DNS TTL churn observed. Affected region: eu-west-1. Pager: @oncall-netops. Link: https://ops.example.com/alerts/ALERT-1769123456 :rotating_light:
Asha Patel: on it, pulling logs and target-health. paging net-eng too. tagging @Ben Cho and @Sophie Liu.
Ben Cho: looking. initial check: NLB target health shows flapping targets in orchard-dedicated-tg-1. could be backend proxy overloaded or security-group rejecting keepalives.
Ben Cho: run aws check: ```bash
aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:eu-west-1:123456789012:targetgroup/orchard-dedicated-tg-1/abcdef --region eu-west-1
```
Ben Cho: sample output: ```
{ "TargetHealthDescriptions": [ { "Target": { "Id": "10.2.5.12", "Port": 8080 }, "TargetHealth": { "State": "unhealthy", "Description": "Connection timed out" } }, { "Target": { "Id": "10.2.5.13", "Port": 8080 }, "TargetHealth": { "State": "healthy", "Description": "OK" } } ] }
```
Sophie Liu: Customer impact? Marco (CSM), do we have a running ticket?
Marco (CSM): Orchard reports API timeouts for a subset of tenants on their EU cluster since ~08:25 UTC. They see ~25% of requests 5xx, primarily auth and upload endpoints. They've started routing some retries client-side. They're asking for ETA and mitigation.
Asha Patel: quick hypothesis: NLB fronting proxy pool hit connection limits on a subset of targets -> failure to accept new connections -> 5xx. Plan: shift a portion of traffic to a warmed standby proxy pool (orchard-proxy-2) in same VPC, update Route53 weighted records, open SG to allow NLB->proxy, and reduce ALB deregistration delay. Rolling config change, low-risk.
Evan Kim: we should also check if security group rule change was recently applied by infra-as-code. I see a Terraform PR merged 07:58 UTC touching orchard-sg that added a deny for ephemeral ports. rolling that back might be faster. @Ben any diffs?
Ben Cho: checking git history... PR #4892 touched orchard-sg inbound rules at 07:56, changed allowed source range for proxy listeners. reverting looks likely. but reverting infra has drift risk; prefer traffic shift to standby proxy first.
Sophie Liu: how fast can we shift? Route53 change with low TTL (30s) should be quick. what's current TTL?
Ben Cho: currently TTL=300. We'll create a weighted record for orchard-api.orchard.example -> set weight 0 for prod target and 100 for orchard-proxy-2, then decrease TTL to 30 during window.
Ben Cho: change commands: ```bash
# lower TTL
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z012345678 --change-batch '{"Changes":[{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"orchard-api.orchard.example","Type":"A","TTL":30,"SetIdentifier":"prod","Weight":100,"ResourceRecords":[{"Value":"3.3.3.3"}]}}]}'
# create weighted record for standby (proxy-2) with weight 0 initially
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z012345678 --change-batch '{"Changes":[{"Action":"CREATE","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"orchard-api.orchard.example","Type":"A","TTL":30,"SetIdentifier":"standby-proxy-2","Weight":0,"ResourceRecords":[{"Value":"3.3.3.77"}]}}]}'
```
deploy-bot: change set cs-orchard-1769 created for Route53 updates by @Ben Cho. runbook: https://runbooks.example.com/orchard/egress-proxy-shift
Asha Patel: I'll coordinate apply. Ben, when you flip weight to 100 for standby, monitor 5xx rate and NLB target health. Also open SG rule to allow 8080 from NLB's IP range if needed.
Ben Cho: applying now. ```bash
# set standby to 100 weight
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z012345678 --change-batch '{"Changes":[{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"orchard-api.orchard.example","Type":"A","TTL":30,"SetIdentifier":"standby-proxy-2","Weight":100,"ResourceRecords":[{"Value":"3.3.3.77"}]}}]}'
```
Ben Cho: applied. deploy-bot: change cs-orchard-1769 executed by Ben Cho.
incident-bot: Alert follow-up: traffic shift executed at 08:34:12 UTC.
Sophie Liu: seeing 5xx drop to ~5% within 40s, and overall latency back to normal. Nice.
Asha Patel: I also adjusted ALB target group deregistration delay from 300 -> 10 to speed draining: ```bash
aws elbv2 modify-target-group-attributes --target-group-arn arn:... --attributes Key=deregistration_delay.timeout_seconds,Value=10
```
Evan Kim: I pushed a temporary SG change to allow NLB -> proxy-2 on 8080 from 10.0.0.0/8 (orchard VPC range). Reverting to tighter CIDR after stable.
Marco (CSM): Orchard confirmed degraded traffic subsided at 08:35 and their teams report successful retries. They want a short incident update and ETA for permanent fix.
Asha Patel: immediate mitigation complete. Next steps: 1) keep traffic split for 1 hour, 2) investigate root cause (proxy capacity vs ephemeral port block from recent TF change), 3) schedule fortnight postmortem with Orchard, 4) prepare rollback playbook to rejoin prod once we confirm target stability.
Ben Cho: capturing logs and kernel connection stats from proxy-1 instances, will attach to incident ticket. ```bash
# quick conntrack-ish check (netstat)
sudo ss -s
```
Sophie Liu: I'm taking handoff for the 08:40-16:40 UTC oncall window. Handoff notes: mitigation in place, watch 5xx, keep SG change temporary, do not revert Route53 until stable for 30m.
Asha Patel: thx. I'll file incident ticket and schedule postmortem. tagging @incident-bot to create incident doc.
incident-bot: Incident created: INCIDENT-2026-ORCHARD-01. Postmortem draft: https://incidents.example.com/INCIDENT-2026-ORCHARD-01
deploy-bot: I created rollback change set cs-orchard-1769-rollback (ready). Apply only after signoff.
Ben Cho: final note: customer deployed a client update at 07:50 that increased concurrent connections per user; combined with the TF SG change that narrowed ephemeral port range, we observed connection saturation on proxy-1. Root cause hypothesis = capacity + SG restriction.
Marco (CSM): Orchard accepts mitigation. They asked for a timeline for permanent capacity bump + SG revert. I'll coordinate.
Sophie Liu: handing over oncall. leaving monitoring alerts for 5xx > 10% to page.
Asha Patel: thanks team. We'll run RCA and include infra change gating in follow-up. Closing the live thread, will update incident doc with attachments. :white_check_mark:
